purpose: The active Change-first Inspector may only import modules that preserve Change/Revision semantics or are explicitly adapted to its bounded reader contract. This inventory keeps retained presentation work visible while preventing the old aggregate-reader composition from returning through an incidental import.
keyboardAndFocusOwnership: change-inspector.ts owns Change-first route intent and bounded read epochs. change-inspector-interaction.ts owns the local Change cursor, Change-first shortcuts, its palette/help dialogs, reader-local display controls, and route-transition focus entry/restoration after each DOM paint. auth.ts separately owns reconnect-dialog settlement, its focus trap, and focus restoration so authentication cannot be hidden while its request remains pending. change-inspector-render.ts owns focusable Change/Revision reading controls plus exact fact/file anchor focus inside the projected detail. Legacy keyboard, palette, detail, diff-controller, render, and main modules remain outside that composition until each is explicitly adapted with Change-first tests.

modules.reason: Owns capability recovery and the reconnect dialog's settlement, focus trap, and focus restoration. The Change-first interaction controller deliberately does not hide or settle that auth-owned dialog.
Owns only Change-first keyboard, route focus, palette/help dialogs, split, reading-mode, theme, and density behavior. Its local cursor can open a Change but never selects a Revision implicitly.
Reads the legacy selected-event/revision aggregate store and fetches legacy revision composites. Exact Change/Revision detail now comes only from change-inspector-reading.ts.
Its route, selection, and snapshot lifecycle are coupled to the legacy aggregate store. The active reader renders only an exact captured resource validated by the Change-first protocol.
Global shortcuts advance legacy Timeline/Revision cursors. Change-first keyboard behavior must be adapted from explicit Change and exact-Revision controls.
Theme and density are reader-local display preferences; they neither fetch nor infer review semantics. Active composition may import only this model-neutral preference surface.
Defines only server-provided supersession graph geometry. Both retained legacy readers and active Change-first fact cards may consume this neutral wire contract without reaching the aggregate store.
Its command set targets legacy entity, lens, and selection state. It may be adapted only after Change-first command and focus contracts exist.
The legacy store subscriber paints aggregate Timeline and Revision semantics. change-inspector-render.ts is the active bounded projection renderer.
Legacy aggregate composition root retained solely for its isolated historical tests; entry.ts is the sole served Change-first composition root.
